ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L561-1 through L561-50-2 and R561-1 through R561-38; Décret n°2018-799 of 20 September 2018 on beneficial ownership; EU Anti-Money-Laundering Directives (EU) 2015/849 and (EU) 2018/843; Code de commerce Articles L123-1 to L123-9 (trade and companies register, RCS); French TRACFIN obligations

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport of each director, manager, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or French consulate in the document holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the notarial act, followed by sworn French translation; consular legalization if the country is not a Hague Convention signatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the corporate shareholder's certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National companies register or competent corporate registry of the shareholder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus sworn French translation by a French court-approved translator ('traducteur assermenté')

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Recent proof of residential address of the manager and shareholders (utility bill or bank statement, less than three months old)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification of signature and sworn translation into French; if a notary authenticates the copy, the notarial certificate must itself be apostilled or legalized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special power of attorney authorizing a designated corporate representative to execute and file the French SARL incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the grantor's country of residence or, for a corporate shareholder, its lawfully empowered board based on a certified extract of corporate resolutions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus sworn French translation; the document must specify the entity, registered office, capital subscription and signatory capacity

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of all directors, managers, shareholders and UBOs against: (i) domestic PEP indicators under Articles L561-4-1 to L561-6 of the French Monetary and Financial Code; (ii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iii) UN Security Council sanctions; (iv) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list because USD wire and ACH rails are anticipated; and (v) the French national asset-freeze list ('gel des avoirs') administered by the Direction générale du Trésor. Enhanced due diligence must be applied to any PEP or high-risk nationality; a reasoned hit must be escalated to TRACFIN and the underlying incorporation transaction must be held pending clearance. Customer due diligence records must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by INPI; RCS post-registration search via Infogreffe / registre national des entreprises (RNE)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Latin alphabet characters, must not be contrary to French public order, must not be misleading as to the activity, legal form, nationality or official status of the company, and must not infringe an earlier registered trademark or company name. A SARL must legitimately indicate the legal form 'SARL' or 'société à responsabilité limitée' on stationary and commercial documents. For foreign-language names, a documented French transliteration is required where the script is not Latin-based, and the name must be pronounceable in French for oral use.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Crédit (when used to imply a credit institution or banking establishment)
État / République / Ministère / Préfecture / Mairie (when an official connection is implied)
AOC / AOP (protected appellations when used for wine or agricultural products)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a statutory pre-incorporation name reservation system; the name is accepted at RCS registration. The 90-day window represents the practical validity period of a professional name-clearance opinion and trademark pre-search, and the search should be refreshed after that time. If the Greffe or Guichet Unique rejects the proposed name, the applicant receives a written refusal with grounds. The applicant may either (i) submit a new incorporation application with a modified name immediately, or (ii) file a written challenge to the refusal before the President of the competent commercial court (tribunal de commerce) or the competent civil court (tribunal judiciaire, commercial chamber) within 15 days of notification, attaching the refusal notice, draft articles of association, name-clearance report and INPI/RNCS search results. If the court annuls the refusal, the registry is bound to process the registration; if the applicant fails to appeal within 15 days, the refusal becomes final and a new filing must be prepared.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a commercial domiciliation provider registered with the local Chamber of Commerce ('centre d'affaires' regime), for a maximum term of five years under a written domiciliation agreement. The virtual office is acceptable for corporate registration, statutory mailing and KYC correspondence, but it does not displace French economic or tax substance: actual managerial control exercised from France and/or the presence of employees and servers or revenue-generating staff will constitute a permanent establishment or French tax residence irrespective of the registered home office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: approximately 3% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection during the first 12 months of operation for a low-risk non-licensed adtech platform; cumulative probability of approximately 10-15% within a five-year cycle, principally through URSSAF social-security audits, corporate tax audits and random RCS/greffe verification visits. Inspections may occur under Article L711-1 of the French Social Security Code or the French tax audit jurisdiction. The risk would increase materially if material VAT credits are claimed, if the company registers in a residential apartment without actual business use, or if the virtual office is used without a domiciliation contract.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Combined statutory filing component and legal-fee component for UBO analysis and attestation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille fee scale, home-jurisdiction notarial tariff, and French court-approved translator tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: One-year registered office domiciliation contract (centre d'affaires) with legal mail handling
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market commercial lease and secretarial service charge for virtual office address and legal mail reception

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat professional fee for a tailored low-risk AML manual, PEP/sanctions screening procedure and UBO record-keeping templates

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (Law No. 2004-604 of 21 June 2004), Title IX, Book II, Chapter II (Articles L. 223-1 to L. 223-35) governing Société à Responsabilité Limitée
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte authentique de constitution et statuts de la société
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of 1 EUR; no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Pro Forma First Board Resolution: The Board of Directors of the proposed SARL resolves unanimously as follows: 1. To form the Société à Responsabilité Limitée with an initial share capital of 1,000 EUR, subscribed as follows: [Name 1] subscribes to 500 shares, [Name 2] subscribes to 500 shares. 2. To establish the registered office at [Address in France]. 3. To appoint [Name] as Gérant with full legal representation powers. 4. To adopt the Articles of Association in the form presented. 5. To authorize the Gérant to file the incorporation documents with the RCS, obtain necessary registrations, and commence business activities. This resolution is adopted in Paris on [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a qualified French corporate attorney to draft the Acte de Constitution and Articles of Association (Statuts). Specify company object as programmatic advertising and ad exchange platform services, set share capital at 1,000 EUR, appoint manager, and define registered office. Ensure full compliance with the French Commercial Code.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, revise documents and resubmit for authentication within 24 hours

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Act of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the signed Acte de Constitution and Statuts to a French notary for authentication. Verify signatures, ensure compliance, and issue the authentic deed. Pay notary fees and applicable taxes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If discrepancies found, amend and re-notarize the same day

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original authenticated Acte de Constitution, Statuts, and required forms to the Greffe of the relevant Tribunal de Commerce. Pay filing fees. The Greffe registers the company, issues the SIREN number, and provides a certificate of registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If application queried, provide additional documents or information promptly

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the incorporation notice in the Bulletin Officiel des Annonces Civiles et Commerciales (BODACC). Obtain official SIREN, SIRET, and RCS registration number. Register for VAT and social security if applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Follow up with INSEE if publication delayed

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: N/A - No industrial or manufacturing license required for digital ad technology platform

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A - Digital operations involve no physical emissions or waste discharge

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: N/A - No physical office space requiring fire safety or structural inspections

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); online portal impots.gouv.fr, professional space 'Gérer mon espace professionnel'
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not established in France but making taxable supplies in France must register for French VAT by filing Form 1606-SD (Cerfa 15433*04) with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) territorialement compétent or, for non-established entities, the Direction des Non-Résidents (DNR) / Service des Impôts des Entreprises Non-Résidents. The filing must be accompanied by certified constitutional documents, proof of foreign registration, evidence of economic activity, and, where required for third-country entities, a fiscal representative appointment. A valid French VAT ID in format FRAB123456789 is issued within approximately 8–15 working days. For entities with a French fixed establishment, the standard SIREN/SIRET registration through INPI and DGFiP is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a 'check-the-box' regime. An SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS). Certain close-held or qualifying SARLs may elect to be taxed as a partnership (Impôt sur le Revenu, IR) under Article 239 bis AA CGI for a maximum of five fiscal years. New SARLs may elect taxation under IS by filing Form 200-2. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available; instead, anti-hybrid rules in Articles 205, 209, 212 bis CGI apply automatically to align deductions with French taxable outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 (non-established taxable persons must register from first taxable supply; the domestic small-business franchise exemption of EUR 36,600 for services / EUR 85,000 for goods is not a registration threshold)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has implemented mandatory electronic invoicing for all B2B supplies, applicable in phases from September 2026 and September 2027. Invoices are transmitted to DGFiP through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a registered Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) via API in structured formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII). No real-time fiscal stamping or continuous clearance requirement exists in the Italian or Spanish model; however, transaction data must be transmitted within one working day. Businesses may use only certified, compliant software for cash register and billing operations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% French VAT) applies to tangible goods exported outside the EU upon physical export evidenced by customs declaration. For services, including programmatic advertising DSP/SSP services, French VAT is not chargeable where the recipient is a taxable person established in another EU Member State (reverse charge, Article 259-1 CGI) or established outside the EU (place of supply outside France). For B2C digital services supplied to non-EU consumers, no French VAT applies; B2C domestic supplies remain taxable. All export-service claims require documentary proof of recipient establishment, service description, and, for intra-EU B2B, a valid EU VAT identification number.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/ECS) cleared by French customs for tangible goods
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical removal outside the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment confirmation evidencing actual receipt of payment
Commercial invoice with full description, Incoterms, and customs value
For offshore services: service contract, proof of recipient establishment, and, if intra-EU, valid EU VAT ID and reverse-charge notification
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and French Customs may conduct documentary and physical audits of zero-rated transactions, including retrospective clawback of falsely claimed export exemptions. Reassessment restores taxable French VAT at 20%, plus statutory interest of 0.20% per month. Administrative penalties under Article 1729 CGI reach 40% in cases of bad faith and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of law. Criminal prosecution for tax evasion under Articles 1741 and 1743 CGI exposes corporate directors to fines up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to five years. The routine reassessment window is six years, extendable to ten in fraud or undisclosed foreign positions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) — national competent authority for monetary policy, balance-of-payments statistics, and foreign-exchange regulatory reporting; prudential supervision over credit institutions and payment services is exercised jointly through the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro-area regime applies: capital and current account transactions are fully liberalised under Articles L.151-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier). No exchange-control approval is required for inbound equity injection, dividend repatriation, or trade settlement. Profit remittance by a French SARL to non-resident shareholders is subject solely to French dividend withholding tax (25% domestic rate, reduced to 0-15% under applicable tax treaty) and to statistical reporting; no administrative FX conversion or prior authorisation is imposed. Residual obligations concern anti-money-laundering reporting, balance-of-payments statistical declarations filed by the credit institution, and the €10,000 customs declaration threshold for physical cash crossing the border.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France imposes no surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio on export or services receipts, including programmatic advertising revenue. Export proceeds may be retained in EUR or in any foreign currency, may be credited to domiciled or foreign accounts, and may be used freely. The receiving bank must report each transaction to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics using the relevant payment purpose code, but no prior declaration, repatriation period, or conversion mandate applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué pour apports en capital) / Professional Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account / Professional Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability rating: Medium-High as complementary treasury rail, Low as exclusive banking solution. A non-EU offshore EMI without a full EU payment-institution licence cannot lawfully provide payment accounts to a French SARL; the French regime, implementing the Payment Services Directive (EU) 2015/2366 under Article L.521-1 of the Code monétaire et financier, requires an ACPR licence or a valid passport of an EEA licence. European digital EMIs such as Qonto, Revolut Business, and Wise Business are viable for high-volume operational receipts and disbursements, supporting EUR and multi-currency accounts with French or EEA IBANs and SWIFT/SEPA rails. They are not acceptable for the statutory capital-escrow deposit required before RCS registration of the SARL, nor as the principal treasury account for long-term financing, and they may impose lower payment limits and stricter freezing policies during AML review.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute statutory mandate exists for physical attendance under French KYC rules; remote opening via video identification with a qualified eIDAS electronic signature is legally possible for a SARL. In market practice, tier-1 French commercial banks such as BNP Paribas and Société Générale almost always require at least one physical meeting with the gérant or a designated authorised signatory at a French branch before issuing an IBAN. A non-resident gérant of a foreign parent may delegate opening to a resident authorised representative under an apostilled and notarised power of attorney, but the bank retains discretionary compliance rights to require a physical interview. Fintech/EMI accounts can be opened fully remotely with corporate documentation and video-KYC of the ultimate beneficial owners. Practical recommendation: open one tier-1 traditional account for escrow and credit plus one EMI account for operational flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: failure to identify and verify natural persons owning or controlling more than 25% of the SARL, contrary to the French statutory beneficial-owner filing under the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly filed UBO declaration submitted to the Company Registry (RCS) on incorporation and confirmed at onboarding; apostilled certificate of good standing of each UBO; valid passports; signed corporate ownership chart with percentage breakdown; attestation du gérant confirming that no undeclared beneficiaries exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident parent or complex cross-border holding structure outside the EEA creating doubts about economic substance, administrative situs, and ultimate control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents of the parent and all intermediate entities; due-diligence file of the ultimate beneficial owners; group structure diagram; official registry excerpt of the parent; tax residence certificates (certificats de résidence fiscale); audited or management accounts of the parent for the last 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Programmatic AdTech exposure: high-velocity, low-ticket transactions to multiple DSP/SSP platforms and data intermediaries suggesting undisclosed principal flows, invoice-booking mismatches, or a discrepancy between declared revenue and transaction frequency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed platform and SSP access agreements (Google DV360, The Trade Desk, Amazon Ads, among others) and RFP/order confirmations; 12-month treasury forecast showing expected transaction counts and average tickets; contractual invoice trail among platform, SSP, agency, and the SARL; sample programmatic auction and activity reports; corporate AML and treasury policy of the business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the share-capital subscription or subsequent shareholder loans originating from a non-EU jurisdiction, indicating possible financing of terrorism or sanctions exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statement of the shareholder evidencing the originating account for the capital deposit; source-of-wealth statement with supporting sale or exit documentation where applicable; sworn affidavit of the shareholder; apostilled signatures; OFAC/EU/ONU sanctions screening of all parties; proof of the originating financial institution's licence and supervisory status.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The SARL statutory capital and any shareholder contribution must first be credited to a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) held with a licensed French credit institution or a notary. The contributing foreign shareholder must wire via SWIFT MT103, or via SEPA Credit Transfer if the shareholder is in the eurozone, quoting the payment purpose word 'EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION / APPORTS EN CAPITAL — SARL CONSTITUTION' and referencing in field 70 the exact wording 'COMPTE BLOQUÉ PRÉALABLE [SARL NAME] — [NOTARY OR BANK NAME]'. The bank's IBAN of the blocked account must be stated precisely, and mis-tagging inbound equity as trade invoice, remuneration, or loan is strictly avoided as it triggers a Banque de France balance-of-payments purpose-code mismatch. After the manager's declaration of subscription and payment (déclaration de souscription et de versement) and RCS registration, the bank releases the funds to the SARL's current operational account. The credit institution files the statistical liaison financière declaration with the Banque de France; no prior administrative authority approval is required and no cross-border restrictions apply to the EUR.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR disbursements within the eurozone use SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and, for urgent low-value payments, SEPA Instant (SCT Inst); euro payments outside the SEPA zone clear via Target2 and SWIFT MT103. Non-EUR settlements, chiefly USD invoices from ad exchanges, data licensing, and fulfilment providers, must be made by SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer, or MT202 COV where cover is separate, inserting the supplier invoice number and contract reference in field 70. A Commercial Letter of Credit is confined to high-value hardware or licence procurement and is unsuitable for DSP/SSP programmatic campaign payments, which are settled via commercial credit cards, virtual cards, or direct invoice agents. The beneficiary IBAN and BIC must match exactly the supplier's banking details; any third-party-payment instruction triggers enhanced AML review. Payment orders are subject to the Target2 and SEPA Regulation (EU) 260/2012 rules, and pre-validation of the beneficiary account is mandated to avoid MT103 rejection.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign-exchange contract (change à terme) with a licensed French credit institution, fully covered by the EUR base currency and underlying commercial exposure
FX swap (swap de change) combining spot and forward legs for EUR/USD and EUR/GBP treasury matching
Cross-currency swap for long-term financing or intercompany loan mismatch hedging
Plain-vanilla EUR/USD or EUR/GBP FX option with premium paid upfront; zero-premium structures are discouraged under MiFID II product governance for corporate clients

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only in exceptional circumstances where one leg is in a non-convertible currency; they are generally absent and ineligible in France for EUR base currency given full convertibility, and any hedging mandate must be documented in the SARL treasury policy and subordinated to the corporate anti-speculation rule

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce) via the Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved by the shareholders within six months after financial year-end and filed within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered filing, potential fine of up to EUR 1,500 or EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance, and possible director liability; persistent non-compliance may trigger judicial enforcement but does not automatically cause administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and tax package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end, or by the second business day after 1 May for a 31 December year-end, subject to the applicable electronic filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month and a 10% surcharge, increasing in cases of formal notice, concealment, or fraudulent conduct

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax annual reconciliation or final annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CA12 annual return generally due within three months after the end of the financial year for the simplified regime; businesses under the normal regime generally file recurring CA3 returns rather than one annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge generally 10%, with interest at 0.20% per month and additional penalties for inaccurate or fraudulent reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally payable by 15 December each year through the business tax account; the initial property declaration is generally filed using Form 1447-C by the statutory first-year deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest and a 5% surcharge generally apply, subject to statutory exceptions and local tax administration rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No routine annual confirmation is generally required; changes to beneficial ownership or control information must generally be reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccurate information may result in criminal penalties for the legal representative, registry injunctions, and restrictions on access to certain business formalities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting minutes and management report, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained at the registered office; filed with the Commercial Court Registry only where a separate filing obligation applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval must generally occur within six months after financial year-end; minutes must be prepared and retained promptly after the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or document the approval meeting may create director liability, shareholder remedies, and court-ordered compliance; it does not automatically trigger administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for a SARL exceeding at least two of the following thresholds at the relevant reference dates: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional mandatory audit rules may apply to certain parent, subsidiary, or controlled-company structures and where shareholders holding at least one-tenth of the capital request a judicial appointment.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority (Autorité des normes comptables), with IFRS generally relevant to listed groups and permitted or required for specified consolidated-accounting circumstances

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France generally does not require a separate annual beneficial ownership confirmation. The SARL must monitor ownership and control continuously and file an updated beneficial ownership declaration within 30 days after any reportable change, including share transfers, voting-right changes, or changes in the natural persons exercising control.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members or share-transfer records
Minute Book of shareholder and management decisions
Annual financial statements and supporting accounting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Typically EUR 600-1,800 annually, approximately USD 650-1,950, depending on location and services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Typically EUR 3,000-10,000 annually, approximately USD 3,250-10,850, depending on turnover, transaction volume, consolidation, and reporting complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.0% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS); reduced 15.0% on the first EUR 42,500 of annual taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (previous-year turnover under EUR 10,000,000) with residual profit taxed at 25.0%; an additional 3.3% social contribution applies when the annual IS liability exceeds EUR 763,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research Tax Credit (CIR): 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100,000,000 and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit (CII): 20% of eligible innovation expenditure up to EUR 400,000; Patent Box (régime de la propriété intellectuelle): 10% reduced rate on the net qualifying income from patents and certifiable IP assets; JEI (young innovative company) status: full IS exemption for the first 36 months then 50% exemption in years 4-6 on profit capped at EUR 200,000; group tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) accessible for members of 95%+ owned French subgroups; no AdTech-specific incentive; DSP/SSP commissions constitute ordinary trading income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite) carryforward subject to the annual cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable base exceeding EUR 1,000,000; optional one-year carryback limited to EUR 1,000,000; only French permanent-establishment losses are reportable.
